synonimy: Immunoglobulin G2, anti-(interleukin 31 receptor A) (human-Mus musculus monoclonal CIM331 gamma-chain), disulfide with human-Mus musculus monoclonal CIM331 kappa-chain, dimer
sekcje: Drug Levels and Effects > Summary of Use during Lactation

No information is available on the use of nemolizumab during breastfeeding. Because nemolizumab is a large protein molecule with a molecular weight of about 144,000 Da, the amount in milk is likely to be very low. It is also likely to be partially destroyed in the infant’s gastrointestinal tract and absorption by the infant is probably minimal. Until more data become available, nemolizumab should be used with caution during breastfeeding, especially while nursing a newborn or preterm infant. Waiting for at least 2 weeks postpartum to resume therapy may minimize transfer to the infant. Elevated serum prolactin and galactorrhea has been reported during therapy in a nonlactating patient.

Drug Levels and Effects > Effects on Lactation and Breastmilk

A 14-year-old girl developed galactorrhea after the initiation of nemolizumab, which became progressively worse with each successive dose. Galactorrhea temporarily resolved when the dosing interval was extended and symptoms gradually improved after drug discontinuation. The patient’s serum prolactin was also elevated and returned to the normal range after drug discontinuation. The symptoms probably were caused by nemolizumab.
